name: Estonia: participant-facing document QC
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/estonia/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026), with the QC sections of the Estonia population guides in C4
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

sections.title: Trial content
sections.instruction: Every participant-facing statement matches the current protocol and other approved trial documents.

items.check: Trial title and EU CT number are correct and match the protocol and CTIS.
Investigational product, comparator and randomisation are described as in the protocol and IB/SmPC.
Visit schedule and study duration match the protocol.
Invasive procedures and sample collections match the protocol.
Optional procedures are identified as optional and match the protocol.
Contraception and pregnancy precautions match the protocol.
Foreseeable risks and burdens match the protocol, IB and current safety information; risk wording is not softened.
Expected benefits and alternatives are stated, including when no direct benefit is expected.
Withdrawal procedures are described.
Injury, insurance and medical-care wording matches the insurance certificate (EE-O1).
Participant contacts for study questions, safety concerns and participant rights are given.
No procedure, benefit or risk statement is added that the protocol or other source documents do not support.

sections.title: Protocol-to-document consistency
sections.instruction: Compare the PIS/ICF directly with the protocol rather than reviewing it in isolation.

items.check: Visit counts, time commitments, treatment periods and follow-up use the same logic as the protocol.
Blood volumes, imaging, biopsies and washouts use the same logic as the protocol.
Prohibited medicines and pregnancy testing use the same logic as the protocol.
Participants receive only information relevant to the pathway they may enter (cohorts, dose levels, optional substudies).
items.applies_when: protocol has several cohorts, dose levels or optional substudies

items.check: The default adult form follows the Estonia patient information and consent guide as baseline.
Each consent choice is understandable and linked to a real activity.
The main trial consent is not conditioned on optional future research, optional genetics, optional sample storage or optional data use unless the protocol and law genuinely require that activity.
Separate consent choices are offered for trial participation and for use of pseudonymised health data or biological samples (Estonian ethics guidance).

The consent record is signed and dated by the participant or legal representative and by the person conducting the consent interview (Article 29); a digital signature valid under Estonian law is supported.

The document states that before consent the participant or representative speaks with a trial-team member who is a doctor, nurse or pharmacist with thorough knowledge of the trial and IMP, has adequate time to decide and receives a copy.
The approved remote-consent process includes video interaction, electronic identification, full opportunity for questions and a valid signature, and has prior Ethics Committee approval.
Voluntary participation and withdrawal are explained, including what happens after withdrawal.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Map the protocol population against the actual document set.

items.check: Every protocol population and inclusion pathway maps to a document set (population × document table).

Healthy volunteers: explains why healthy volunteers are needed, no direct medical benefit, screening and exclusion, confinement, restrictions, blood-draw burden, safety monitoring, incidental findings and follow-up after withdrawal; a dedicated document when patients are also enrolled or procedures, risk-benefit, payment or screening differ materially.

Minors: every age band in the protocol has a matching information document; ages 7 to 17 have a consent pathway for both the minor and the legal representative, with each decision and signature clear (not a mere acknowledgement by the minor).
Minors: child language is developmentally appropriate; dissent and withdrawal are explained; signatures match the legal pathway (no assumed two-parent rule); re-consent at adulthood planned.

Incapacitated adults: the protocol permits inclusion; representative authority handled at site level; participant information adapted to capacity; presumed intent addressed; dissent and withdrawal respected; re-consent planned if capacity changes.

Emergency enrolment: every Article 35 condition is satisfied; emergency identification is operational; the representative search fits the therapeutic window; later consent is sought without undue delay; refusal and withdrawal are meaningful; child or incapacity rules layered on when relevant; data and samples collected before later consent are handled consistently.

Impartial witness: the trigger is defined; witness independence protected; selection and role explained; signature blocks cover participant or representative, interviewer and witness; the witness is not described as the legal decision-maker; the participant receives a copy.

Pregnancy follow-up: participant and partner scenarios use different document logic; only necessary pregnancy and infant data requested; follow-up duration defined; medical-record access wording matches the real Estonian pathway.

Secondary use: future use clearly separate from required protocol use; optional choices not bundled with the main participation decision; refusing future use does not prevent main-trial participation.

sections.title: Data privacy
sections.instruction: The PIS/ICF explains the actual data flow rather than generic privacy language.

items.check: Categories of personal and health data are stated.
Who collects and controls the data, and who may access coded source data, are stated.
Pseudonymisation is explained.
Transfers outside Estonia or the EEA are described.
items.applies_when: data transferred outside Estonia or the EEA

items.check: Retention, monitoring and audit access are explained.
Withdrawal consequences for data are stated realistically.
Optional future research with data is described as a separate choice.
Participant rights and contacts are given.
The document does not state that trial-participation consent is automatically the legal basis for all GDPR processing.
Source-data access wording is realistic: sponsor representatives do not automatically gain direct access to Estonia's national Health Information System.
What is collected and for what purpose.
Coding status (pseudonymised or anonymised).
Transport and storage location.
Retention duration in years and destruction plan.
Whether genetic analysis is involved.
Whether future use is optional.
Whether samples may leave Estonia or the EEA.
Consistent with the EU biological-sample compliance form (EE-S1).
Compensation and reimbursement information is in the ICF, not in recruitment advertising.
Unavoidable direct trial expenses are reimbursed according to the approved plan, and the reimbursement principles are explained.

Compensation for time or burden is offered only to competent adults, with basis and amount justified in the application and approved by the Ethics Committee (healthy volunteers: time based on the Estonian minimum wage in the year the trial was initiated); not dependent on risk.
No completion bonus and no large share of payment deferred to the end as an incentive to stay enrolled.

Incapacitated participants and their representatives, minors and their representatives, pregnant women and breastfeeding women receive only reimbursement of direct costs, not participation compensation.
Amounts and conditions match P1 (EE-P1).
The Estonian participant-facing version is present.
A complete version is present in every other language in which the material will be used with participants.
Every participant-facing item includes the EU CT number.
'Participant' is used instead of 'patient' as the national guidance requests.
The national ICF template has been considered.
The current CTIS placement rule for Estonian-language patient-facing materials has been followed (multinational: Part II section R; mononational: EU Q&A route).
Reimbursement and compensation wording follows Estonia guidance.
Data protection is explained in detail.
Sample handling is described.
No drafting instruction remains ([bracket] notes, italic notes, '...........' gaps, yellow form labels).
Clear version number and date.
Consistent trial identifier and sponsor name.
Consistent site name.
Signature blocks match the actual consent pathway.
No pre-signed participant signature on a blank submission template.
Correct language label.
No tracked changes or drafting comments in the clean submission version.
Plain Estonian suitable for the target participant population.
The English master is not used as the participant document unless English will genuinely be used with a specific participant group.
Headings explain the decision being made.
Abbreviations are defined.
Risks are not hidden in dense paragraphs.
Optional choices are visually separate from mandatory trial participation.
Child documents are adapted to age and maturity rather than a mechanically shortened adult form.
